chunk_map.heading: H1/lede: Map the access surface, own the delta
Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk
Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map
Point the skill at your feature
Kick off the pass, then work the other window
Phase 2: Read the map back before you decide the delta
Phase 3: Add the surface the skill over-called, and the one it missed
Push back until the reason names your codebase
Phase 4: Add the context header a cold reader needs

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 4 "Kick off the pass, then work the other window" L52 "Switch to your m3-quality window now." — "m3-quality" is not named anywhere earlier in THIS file (chunk 0's Window widget names only "m3-security"). Verified against the sibling exercise the module includes immediately before this one: `curriculum/exercises/open-the-side-quest.md:39,42` has the student run `/rename m3-quality` on the second worktree session — a student-produced session artifact from the immediately-prior exercise in `earn-the-trust.md`'s Start Here order (line 33 vs line 37). Falls under both the session-artifact carve-out and the module-include-order carve-out; not a violation despite the maintainer's 2026-08-25 lean pass cutting the connecting sentence ("Both windows are already open from Open the side quest…") that used to spell this out explicitly. Also checked: "STRIDE" (chunk 0 L11, reused chunk 1/8/9) is named in the enclosing module's What-You'll-Learn bullet 2 before this exercise's include, so arc-earned; "the delta" (title + chunks 1,6,7,9) self-earns at chunk 0 ("own the delta", "What you build"); "The countermove from M1" (chunk 1 L18) unpacks in the same sentence and "M1" is a module name (explicitly carved out). No unresolved pronoun/demonstrative found in any chunk.

Closest candidate: chunk 3 L47 "The plan path you noted at Module 2's close is the best input here." Locates a fact by module-close position, but the enclosing module's own Prework (`earn-the-trust.md:12`, "you noted the path at M2 close") establishes this identically before the exercise is reached — module-include-order carve-out, not an invented positional pointer. "The countermove from M1" (chunk 1 L18) is unpacked in the same sentence ("tell the agent what output you want") — passes the named-not-located test. "Author your test-strategy skill" (chunk 4 L52) and "the STRIDE exercise" (chunk 9 L94) are both named by title, matching real files (`author-test-strategy-skill.md`, `threat-model-with-stride.md`) listed in the module's Start Here order — not positional ("the next exercise"), and forward-pointing by name is not what §2 bans.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: na_reason: no guess/predict-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body — this is a skill-invocation-and-review exercise, not a prediction beat.

Closest candidate: chunk 7 "Push back until the reason names your codebase" (lines 80-82, 33 words per `check-slide-size.js --report`) — one bullet, but it carries a full self-standing claim plus a worked contrast example ("'The billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry...' beats 'webhooks need auth.'"), not a bare wait-state bullet. Chunk 4 (the other short chunk, 96 words/2 bullets) is substantive (names the two-window move and gives the switch instruction). No chunk is content-free or purely context-dependent.

chunk 2 "Phase 1: Run the curated skill on your feature and save the map" (lines 22-39): the header promises two actions (run the curated skill on the student's feature; save the map). The chunk's actual content (lines 24-39, confirmed against current body: the `/skills` command, "you should see access-control-analysis and stride listed under User," and prompt-1 "List my installed skills...") only performs skill discovery/listing. The actual invoke-on-feature-and-save-to-disk action is in prompt-2, under the NEXT `##` heading "Point the skill at your feature" (lines 41-47), which carries no "Phase 1" framing of its own. Under the projected sequential slide read, the Phase 1 slide's own content contradicts what its header claims it does. Harm check: a trainer or self-study reader in Slides view could read the Phase 1 header as already covering invoke+save, then be confused when the actual invoke/save prompt appears on a differently-titled slide with no Phase-1-continued marker — the exact failure §6 generalizes `check_writing.md §18` to catch, and one long-read would not surface (there the two `##` sections read as one continuous phase). This chunk boundary is untouched by the 2026-08-25 lean-pass diff, so this is not new: the prior slides instance (body_sha 070bd331…, pre-dating this session's edits) flagged the identical chunk/header pair as REVISE/non-blocking; independently re-verified against the current body rather than carried from that cache.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Retitle chunk 2 to what it actually delivers this slide (e.g. "Phase 1: Confirm the skill is on hand"), or move the invoke-and-save prompt into this chunk so the header's promise lands on the slide that carries it.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all five sub-items across all 10 chunks. (a) `grep -niE 'not [a-z].*\. not [a-z].*\.'` on body.txt → 0 hits, no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction. (b) no anaphora/epistrophe triples found on manual read. (c) self-grading-superlative grep (`one of the most|most useful|most important|game.?chang|powerful move|critical(ly)?|essential`) → 0 hits in body; closest candidate chunk 0 L11 "STRIDE without an access-surface map is pub-quiz threat modeling" is a stance claim about the field (backing block classifies it as a position, not a value-prop claim about this exercise), not a self-grading superlative. (d) no number-with-retraction pattern; the only numbers in body are widget timings (20/7/3 min) with no hedge/retraction attached. (e) no abstraction-noun-stack or empty-leg verb triplet — prose stays concrete throughout (e.g. "the billing webhook re-hits the queue on retry").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|connections)\b' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--map-the-access-surface.body.txt` → all matches are on "surface"/"access-surface"/"surface map" (9 hits); zero hits for firing/compendium/forcing function/beat/mood/Connections in the body region. "Surface" here is the exercise's own domain term (attack/access-surface analysis, a real security-engineering concept, not the compendium's banned authorial-jargon sense "writing surface"). "Delta" is ordinary engineering usage (diff between two reads).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold usage confined to: chunk 0's widget-chrome labels (Time/Window/What you do/What you build/The point — the file's own maintainer block explicitly calls these chrome, not emphasis, per its "**Emphasis:**" note); chunk 2's single handle **User** (L30); chunk 6's delta-menu pair **The over-call.** / **The miss.** (L68-69) — two bolded leads on one slide, explicitly documented in the same maintainer note as "one handle per item on the Phase 3 menu slide," matching §9's reading-list/menu-slide carve-out (budget lifted, handle-cap still respected — each handle ≤3 words); chunk 8's **What happened:** — widget chrome per the same maintainer note. No bolded-lead monoculture anywhere; ordinary bullets elsewhere are plain prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 8 of 9 `##` headings are unambiguously imperative ("Take the ranked ten...", "Point the skill at your feature", "Kick off the pass...", "Push back until...") or "Phase N:" + imperative. Closest candidate: chunk 9 "What this sets up" (line 92) is neither imperative nor a Phase label, but asserts no generalizable law/claim (unlike the compendium's declarative specimens, e.g. "Anything can be reverse-engineered") — it functions as a navigational segue naming what the next exercise depends on, matching the orientation-header carve-out ("You are here"). `grep -rn '^## What this sets up' curriculum/exercises/*.md` shows the identical heading reused verbatim in `author-test-strategy-skill.md:69`, confirming a repeated closer-label convention in the exercise library, not a one-off ambiguity. Judge-owned classification note: rules 15 and 16 postdate the template's blocking/non-blocking partition (which only lists rules 1-14); applying the template's own stated principle ("I cannot follow this" = blocking, "this could be tighter" = TODO), a wrong-mood heading is a genre/polish mismatch, not a comprehension failure — classified non-blocking here, sibling to rule 6 (also header-scoped, also non-blocking).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bullet against the three classes. Accept-noted: chunk 9's closer ("The STRIDE exercise invokes the curated STRIDE skill on the map you just built... if you worked the delta, STRIDE has something real to chew on," lines 92-94) is explicitly cleared in the maintainer block ("Carded and kept (Antti 2026-08-25): the *What this sets up* slide — the sow-here-reap-at-STRIDE motivation stays; do not re-card") — not flagged. Closest un-accepted candidate: chunk 4 L51 "That wait is the two-window move Module 3 installs" names the module's own design pattern (self-referential flavor), but it stays inside class (b) because the clause is fused to a concrete instruction in the same sentence ("kick off a long task in one window, do active work in the other, come back when the first lands") and this is the FIRST operationalization of the two-window move in this file, not a redundant re-announcement of work already done — unlike the banned specimens ("You encounter the problems before the training names them"), which carry no instruction at all. The 2026-08-25 lean-pass diff itself independently confirms the rule is being actively applied to this file: the maintainer's own cut-list names "aphorism kicker, §16c" for the removed "One sentence buys the time back" line and a "forward plant" / "restatement" for three other removed lines, and a re-check of the current body against those same three classes found no further instance.
